pamphlet_excerpts: A properly working plumbing system protects: Plumbing systems carry water into and out of a home through a system of pipes (p. 20).

A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 2: For the health and safety of the people wholive there, the water entering the home through the water-supplysystem must be pure and clean (p. 20).
A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 3: Wastewater should never come into contact with the water that the family uses for drinking, bathing, or washing clothes anddishes (p. 20).

Step 2 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Theseregulations, commonly called plumbing codes, are important inpreventing the water-supply system from becoming contaminated (p. 20).
Step 3 (A properly working plumbing system protects): National plumbing codes exist that give specific regulations for all plumbingoperations (p. 20).
Step 4 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Many communities have adopted these regulationsor amended them to fit their local needs (p. 20).

Step 3 (Plumbing Applied Field Standard): Step 3 (Make A Drawing): The pressure comes from a pump (if the water comes from a well) or from gravity (if the water comes from a water tower or reservoir) (p. 9).
Step 4 (Plumbing Applied Field Standard): Step 4 (Make A Drawing): When you flush a toilet or pull the plug from a bathtub, gravity pulls the waste and water down and away from the house (p. 9).
